definitions.definition: For a periodic integrable f, hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx. The transform extends by completion to Sobolev spaces and by distributional duality. Reality means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0.

definitions.type: family of Fourier Sobolev spaces and norms
definitions.definition: For real s, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2), ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. H^s is the completion of trigonometric polynomials, interpreted as distributions for negative s; L2=H^0 with the normalized spatial norm. On mean-zero functions ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. Time suprema use continuous representatives and derivative norms essential suprema. For sequences x, ||x||_(ell2)^2=sum_k |x(k)|^2; ell1 uses sum_k |x(k)|. Frequency projections P_{<=A}, P_{>A} retain respectively |k|<=A and |k|>A.
S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k), for every real t.
Dinv=D^(-1)=partial_x^(-1): its multiplier is (i*k)^(-1) at k!=0 and zero at k=0. D^(-2)=Dinv composed with Dinv. Spatial derivatives use multiplier i*k.

definitions.type: normalized periodic KdV equation and exact-solution convention
definitions.definition: KdV is the equation u_t+partial_x^3 u=(1/2)*partial_x(u^2) on mathbbT. For a real mean-zero datum q in H^s, s>=0, and horizon A>0, an exact solution u with datum q means the real mean-zero C([0,A];H^s) distributional solution of this equation with u(0)=q obtained by smooth approximation. An exact twisted solution v means v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) for this same equation and interval. A smooth exact solution means such a solution with smooth space and time dependence. These terms specify a solution relation only; existence, uniqueness, bounds and the differential equation for the twist are proved, rather than granted by this definition.

inputs.statement: For the real mean-zero 2*pi-periodic source equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx, with normalized homogeneous norms, the following results hold in its norm-preserving twisted representation. For every s>=0, time horizon A>0 and L2 upper bound B0, Galerkin solutions with datum q in dot H^s and ||q||_2<=B0 obey sup_[0,A]||U_m||_(dot H^s)<=M_s, uniformly in m, with M_s depending only on s,A,B0,||q||_(dot H^s). For s>0 and 0<sigma<s, a subsequence converges strongly in L^p([0,A];H^sigma), 1<p<infinity, and weak-star in L^infty dot H^s to a distributional solution with the same bound and L2 conservation a.e.. This solution is unique, is C([0,A];dot H^s), preserves L2 at every time and depends Lipschitz continuously on the datum for s>1/2, and also for 0<s<=1/2. At s=0 there is a unique C([0,A];L2) solution with Lipschitz dependence obtained by smoothing. For theta in (-1,0] and two data q,r in L2 whose norms sum to at most B0, the two twisted flows satisfy sup_[0,A]||Utw-Vtw||_(dot H^theta)<=C' C_(B0)^A ||q-r||_(dot H^theta), where C',C_(B0) depend only on B0,theta.

hypotheses: Data are real, mean zero and in the stated homogeneous spaces on the 2*pi torus.
The horizon is positive, exponent ranges are as stated, and the L2 upper bounds hold.

output.statement: For T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0 there is A=A(T,gamma,R)<infinity such that every real mean-zero datum q in H^gamma with ||q||_(H^gamma)<=R has a unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional solution u of u_t+u_xxx=u*u_x, obtained by smooth approximation, and sup_[0,T]||u||_(H^gamma)<=A. Smooth data give spatially smooth solutions on [0,T]. For two real mean-zero L2 data q,r of norms summing to at most B0, the exact solutions satisfy sup_[0,T]||u_q-u_r||_2<=C(T,B0)||q-r||_2. Twisting v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) preserves all Sobolev norms and for smooth data v'=B_t(v,v)/2. Consequently M=1+sup_[0,T]||v||_(H^gamma)<=1+A uniformly on the datum ball.

argument.text: Fix a real mean-zero q in H^gamma and assume L1: ||q||_(H^gamma)<=R. H001-H003 give T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0. Use E001 for source datum U0(x)=-q(-x), exponent s=gamma and horizon T. Reflection and sign preserve the Fourier Sobolev and L2 norms, so ||U0||_(dot H^gamma)<=R and ||U0||_2<=R. The source yields a global unique continuous flow, its uniform Sobolev bound, and smooth flows when the datum is smooth (apply its positive regularity statements for each integer exponent in that case). Its Galerkin bound and limiting-solution bound are uniform for the prescribed norm bounds.

produces.statement: For the source datum U0(x)=-q(-x) there is a unique continuous homogeneous H^gamma source flow U on [0,T], with uniform bound determined only by T,gamma,R; for smooth q it has every Sobolev regularity.

binders.type: source solution path whose existence is asserted

argument.text: Take that source flow U and set u(t,x)=-U(t,-x). At (t,-x), u_t=-U_t, u_x=U_x and u_xxx=U_xxx, so u_t+u_xxx=-U U_x=u*u_x. Fourier coefficients are hat u(k)=-hat U(-k), preserving reality, zero mean and every Fourier norm. On mean-zero functions and s>=0, |k|<=<k><=sqrt(2)|k|, hence ||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s); for s<0 the inequalities reverse as in the supplied norm convention. The source bound therefore gives some A(T,gamma,R) in our norm. It also holds for a smooth-approximation limit by passing first in each finite Fourier norm sum and then taking the supremum over finite sets. The sign-reflection map is invertible, so uniqueness and continuous dependence transfer. Finally differentiation of v=S_(-t)u cancels the linear KdV term and yields v'=B_t(v,v)/2 for smooth data; the unimodular Fourier symbol of S preserves all norms. Thus M=1+sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=1+A as asserted. This proves the asserted existence, bound, twist identity and solution convention for arbitrary q under L1; discharge L1.

For arbitrary real mean-zero L2 data q1,q2 and B0>=0, temporarily assume L2: ||q1||_2+||q2||_2<=B0. Apply E001's theta=0 dependence statement at time horizon T to -q1(-x),-q2(-x). Their norms and their difference norm are unchanged. The source twists are unitary, so its dependence bound gives sup_[0,T]||u_q1-u_q2||_2<=C(T,B0)||q1-q2||_2 in physical variables after sign-reflection. Discharge L2.
